answer: Earned service credits resist Sybil attacks: each agent starts at zero and gains credit only by completing verified work for others, like a reef growing one polyp at a time. Credit accrues slowly, is capped per epoch, and cannot be bought or moved between identities. Voting weight and task access scale with credit, so a thousand fresh identities are worth no more than one. Reputation is carved in marble, not painted on: misbehavior burns credit permanently, while honest work polishes it like jade. An attacker must pay in real work for every identity, making large-scale fakery uneconomical.
